title: Interactive DR runbook for SLO-prioritized traffic draining and verification
creator: Maya Kapoor
description: Create an interactive, SLO-driven active-passive DR runbook focused on prioritized traffic draining, circuit-breaker choreography, and backup/restore verification. The artifact should enable an on-call engineer or runbook operator to perform a scheduled or ad-hoc passive-region promotion drill with measurable SLO checks, automated KV snapshot validation, and post-drill audits. This ticket covers playbook text, automations (scripts/CI jobs), test harnesses for restore verification, and a canonical checklist for gates and rollback.
background: We maintain active regions with passive warm standbys. Previous drills surfaced gaps: unvalidated snapshot rotation, inconsistent KV indexes after restores, and unclear sequencing between circuit-breaker tripping and traffic drains. We need a repeatable operator flow that prioritizes user-visible SLOs (latency P95 and error rate) during each step and allows automated forensic assertions to detect latent data drift.
goals: Define an operator-friendly runbook that sequences traffic quarantine, circuit-breaker detuning, KV snapshot rehydration, and progressive promotion
Automate backup integrity checks (SHA256) and KV-level read-after-write assertions against a golden prompt set
Measure and enforce SLO gates during the drill (P95 latency, 99th token latency, error rate thresholds)
Provide rollback criteria and automated rollback playbooks if invariants fail
Schedule drill automation in CI with alerting and post-drill reports
acceptance_criteria: Runbook written with step-by-step operator actions and expected metrics for each step
A CI job exists that can run a full passive-promotion drill in staging and produce a pass/fail artifact
Backup files are verified with cryptographic checksums and cataloged; a test restore validates key ranges and a sample of user prompts
Circuit-breaker tuning knobs and their safe default values are documented and applied during the drill
Post-drill audit report template in Confluence is populated by the CI job and includes metric diffs and snapshot hashes
runbook_steps: Pre-check: confirm latest snapshots exist and checksums match the catalog; abort if mismatch
Pre-check: run a dry SLO query against active region; record baseline P50/P95/P99 and error rate
Step 1 (Quarantine): apply region-level traffic quarantine policy to divert new writes to active only; enable read-only flag on passive
Step 2 (Circuit-breaker): gradually reduce circuit-breaker thresholds in passive region to ensure graceful shedding; observe error spike tolerances
Step 3 (Snapshot rehydrate): restore latest KV snapshot into passive region test cluster; run read-after-write assertions for prioritized key prefixes
Step 4 (Canary traffic): route a 1% canary of reads to the restored passive cluster with canary keys; validate response parity and timing against baseline
Step 5 (Progressive promotion): increase traffic to passive in stages (1%, 10%, 50%) while continuously checking SLO gates; halt on failures
Step 6 (Rollback): if any SLO gate or data assertion fails, immediately execute automated rollback to previous routing and initiate forensic snapshot comparison
Step 7 (Post-drill audit): capture metric deltas, store snapshot checksums, collect logs and spans, and file the drill report
validation_tests: SHA256 checksum validation for backup archives and manifest comparison
KV snapshot read-after-write test using a curated prompt/response set; tolerate <=0.1% divergence
End-to-end request parity test for 1000 sampled requests comparing active and restored passive responses
SLO gate monitor: fail if P95 latency increases >25% over baseline or if error rate exceeds 0.5% absolute
Circuit-breaker stress test that simulates slow downstreams and checks for graceful shedding behavior
